title: The Thank-You Seed

pages.text: Joyful Otter found a tiny golden seed by the river. 'I wonder what it grows into?' she said.
pages.narratorLine: Every kind word is like planting a seed.

pages.text: She planted it carefully and whispered, 'Thank you, little seed, for choosing me.' The next morning, a small green sprout appeared with a warm glow.
pages.narratorLine: When we say thank you, kindness starts to grow.

pages.text: 'Wow!' said Otter. 'Gratitude makes things grow!' She decided to say thank you to someone every single day.
pages.narratorLine: Your turn! Who can you thank today?

doAction.instruction: Say 'thank you' to someone who helps you today.
steps: Think of someone who helped you recently.
Tell them 'Thank you!' and say why you're grateful.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Say 'thank you' to someone you love.

shinePrompt: How did it feel to say thank you?

title: Brave Bear's First Step

pages.text: Brave Bear stood at the edge of the Kindness Garden. The path ahead looked different from anything he'd seen before.
pages.narratorLine: Being brave doesn't mean you're not scared.

pages.text: 'What if I make a mistake?' Bear whispered. His golden heart glowed softly. 'Mistakes help me grow,' he remembered.
pages.narratorLine: Your heart knows — trying is what matters most.

pages.text: Bear took one step, then another. With each step, tiny flowers bloomed behind him. 'My courage is making the garden grow!'
pages.narratorLine: Every brave step you take makes the world more beautiful.

doAction.instruction: Try something new or a little bit scary today.
steps: Think of something you've been wanting to try but felt nervous about.
Take a deep breath and try it!

shinePrompt: How did it feel to be brave?

title: The Sharing Acorn

pages.text: Sharing Squirrel had collected the most beautiful acorn in the whole garden. It glowed golden in her tiny paws.
pages.narratorLine: Sometimes the most special things are even better when shared.

pages.text: She saw Gentle Deer sitting alone, looking sad. 'Would you like to hold my special acorn?' Squirrel asked.
pages.narratorLine: Noticing when someone needs kindness — that's having Kind Eyes.

pages.text: Deer's eyes lit up. 'Really? For me?' When they held the acorn together, it glowed twice as bright. Sharing had made it even more special.

doAction.instruction: Share something you enjoy with someone else.
steps: Pick a toy, snack, or activity you like.
Invite someone to enjoy it with you.

shinePrompt: How did sharing make you feel?

pages.text: Dark clouds gathered over the Kindness Garden. Joyful Otter felt something heavy in her chest. 'What is this feeling?' she wondered.
pages.narratorLine: All feelings are okay — even the tricky ones.

pages.text: 'I think I feel... frustrated,' Otter said slowly. Just naming the feeling made it a little smaller. The clouds lightened a tiny bit.
pages.narratorLine: When we name our feelings, they become easier to hold.

pages.text: Otter took three deep breaths. With each breath, a rainbow appeared. 'My feelings are like weather — they come and go, and every one is important.'
pages.narratorLine: You're learning something amazing — feelings are messengers, not monsters.

doAction.instruction: Name three feelings you had today.
steps: Think about your morning — what did you feel?
Think about your afternoon — what feeling visited?
Right now — what feeling is here? Say it out loud.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Tell a grown-up how you feel right now.

title: The Kindness Watering Can

story.title: Gentle Deer Sees a Friend in Need

pages.text: Gentle Deer noticed a small flower in the garden drooping low. No one else seemed to see it. But Deer had Kind Eyes.
pages.narratorLine: Kind Eyes means noticing when someone needs help.

pages.text: 'You look thirsty, little flower,' Deer said softly. She found a watering can and gave the flower a gentle drink.
pages.narratorLine: You don't have to do something big — small kindnesses matter most.

pages.text: The flower stood tall again and bloomed bright pink. 'Thank you for seeing me,' it whispered. Deer smiled. Paying attention was the kindest thing of all.
pages.narratorLine: Today, use your Kind Eyes. Who around you might need a little kindness?

doAction.instruction: Use your Kind Eyes — notice someone who could use a little help or a kind word.
steps: Look around you with Kind Eyes.
Find someone who might need help, a smile, or a kind word.
Do one small kind thing for them.

shinePrompt: Who did your Kind Eyes help today?
